sections.overview: This longhorn beetle is chiefly known as a pest of structural softwood timber.
sections.identification: The French building guide gives adults as 10–20 mm long and cream-colored larvae as 20–25 mm.
sections.habitat: Larvae develop in seasoned conifer wood, especially pine and spruce used in buildings.
sections.diet: Larvae tunnel through the wood; adults do not feed, according to the Argentine pest-monitoring account.
sections.behavior: Adults are short-lived and can walk or fly after emerging from the wood.
sections.reproduction: Females lay eggs in cracks in wood or bark, from which the wood-boring larvae hatch.
sections.ecology: The larval galleries weaken timber; the insect was historically a forest species but is now mainly associated with buildings.
sections.conservation: The consulted sources treat it as a timber pest and provide no wild-species conservation assessment.
